title: Shaping maternal physiology: Immune control of reproductive adaptation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran the paper context tool: Europe PMC reports the paper is not open access, has no PubMed Central ID, no supplementary files, no data flag, no database cross-references and no text-mined accession numbers. Crossref metadata shows a 7-page article (Science 394:46-52) with 65 references and no licence record. A Zenodo search on the DOI returned 0 records. There is no data file anywhere to open.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was available. Its wording ('In this work, we discuss how pregnancy reprograms maternal immunity to orchestrate physiological reprograming of tissues') plus the page range and reference count identify it as a narrative review, not a study that generated measurements.

a1_downloadable.note: FAIL. No dataset of any kind: no supplementary files, no accession numbers (GEO, SRA, BioProject, dbGaP all empty), no Zenodo/Dryad deposit on the DOI, and the full text itself is paywalled with no PubMed Central copy. This is a review article that re-describes other groups' published findings; it produced no new data to download.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessed - stopped at A1. There is no table, so there is no column that could hold a prediction target.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not assessed - stopped at A1. No rows exist; count left null rather than guessed.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the article is a literature review and contributes no measurements, so nothing can be trained or tested on it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use immune cell profiles across pregnancy to predict how a mother's organs adapt - but no data exists here.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would need, per pregnant individual and timepoint, measurements of immune cell types and signalling molecules in blood or tissue. This review supplies none; the number of examples available from it is zero.
plain_idea.predict: Measured changes in maternal organ physiology during pregnancy (for example heart output, insulin sensitivity, or bone turnover), taken from clinical or laboratory assays. This paper reports no such measurements of its own.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Obstetric and reproductive immunology groups would want to know which immune signals forecast maternal adaptation or its failure, but that project would have to be built from the primary studies this review cites, not from the review.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. Any machine learning project on immune control of maternal physiology would have to start from the primary datasets cited inside the review (for example published single-cell atlases of pregnancy), each of which would need its own separate evaluation.

effort.compute_note: No estimates possible: there is no dataset.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether the article has any supplementary files or accession numbers. It has none, and this check took one tool call.

verdict_reason: This is a narrative review in Science (7 pages, 65 references) summarising other groups' work on how the immune system shapes maternal organ adaptation in pregnancy. It generated no data: Europe PMC shows no supplementary files, no accessions and no PubMed Central full text, and a DOI search of Zenodo returned nothing. Part A1 fails outright - there is no file to download, so no later checklist item applies. Reviews are not candidates; the useful follow-up would be to evaluate the primary pregnancy immune atlases it cites, each as its own candidate.
